official.deadline_note: All parts of the file must be complete by 1 November: online registration with the uploaded PDF, both recommendation letters e-mailed after registration, and (for non-Lisbon-Convention qualifications) certified true copies posted with a 1 November postmark. The online application for the 2027/2028 academic year is open and the deadline is 1 November 2026.
official.status_note: UNIL states: 'The online application for the academic year 2027/2028 is open. The deadline is 1 November 2026.'
official.tuition_coverage_note: 'Scholarship recipients are exempt from the standard course registration fees. Only the semester fees of CHF 80 remain payable.'

eligibility: Hold a foreign university degree recognized as equivalent to a Swiss university bachelor's degree before starting the Master's programme at UNIL
Have achieved outstanding academic results during those studies
Minimum language level of C1: French for programmes taught in French, English for programmes taught in English
Not be currently enrolled at UNIL
Have paid the non-refundable administrative fee of CHF 200
Students who have already begun a Master's programme at UNIL or are in the preparatory year are not authorized to apply
Applicants who already hold a foreign master's degree may apply, but priority is given to applicants holding only a bachelor's degree
Withdrawal from the master programme leads to suspension of the scholarship
requirements: Prepare the application file as a single PDF in the prescribed document order
Two letters of recommendation sent directly by their authors from a professional (not private) e-mail address, naming the candidate in full, only accepted if sent after online registration

Certified true copies by post (diplomas, transcripts, provisional certificates in a university-sealed envelope with a cover letter) if the degree comes from a state that has not ratified the Lisbon Convention - and only if the online registration has been submitted

Two letters of recommendation sent directly by their authors to mastergrants@unil.ch from professional e-mail addresses
Certified true copies of diplomas and transcripts in a university-sealed envelope by post, only for qualifications from states that have not ratified the Lisbon Convention

Students whose academic results are of a very high level (there is no list of required grades by country)

official.application_route: One online registration with a single ordered PDF; the same file doubles as the application for admission to the chosen Master's programme - no separate Admissions Office application is needed.
official.citizenship_residency: Exclusively for students who have graduated from a foreign university; applicants must not be currently enrolled at UNIL
official.international_eligibility: Yes - the scholarship exists exclusively for graduates of foreign universities applying to UNIL Master's programmes
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Not open for: Master from the School of Medicine; Master in Sciences and Practices of Education; Master of Law (except the specialisms International and Comparative Law, Legal Theory and International Tax Law and Policy); MSc Physical Education and Sport Didactics; MSc Health Sciences; MSc Sustainable Management & Technology; MSc Human Taphonomy; all MAS programmes. Master in Finance, Psychology, Arts or Nursing carry additional conditions
official.duration: The minimum statutory period of the chosen Master's programme
official.description: UNIL 'awards around ten excellence scholarships each year, exclusively to students who have graduated from a foreign university and whose academic results are of a very high standard', paid at CHF 1,600 per month for the minimum statutory period of the Master's programme, and states the amount 'does not cover the full cost of living in Switzerland'.
official.program_type: University excellence scholarship for international master's admission
official.english_requirement: Minimum C1 in the teaching language. For a Master taught in English (unless mother tongue or a bachelor's entirely taught in English): TOEFL CBT 250, TOEFL IBT 100, TOEFL PBT 600, Academic IELTS 7, Cambridge CAE Grade B, Cambridge CPE Grade C or TOEIC 850; the language diploma should not be older than 2 years. For a Master taught in French: DALF C1/C2, TCF Tout public C1 (all 5 components), CQF (Le Fil de l'EFLE) C1 (four exams) or TELC C1, also under 2 years old. No certificate is required if the programme's language is the candidate's mother tongue or the bachelor's studies were entirely taught in it.

not_confirmed: travel_coverage: no travel benefit is published for the scholarship
verification.notes: Verified on the official UNIL Master's Scholarship page: CHF 1,600 per month for the minimum statutory period, the registration-fee exemption with CHF 80 semester fees, the 1 November 2026 deadline for 2027/2028, the explicit statement that the amount is not full funding (about CHF 2,000/month needed in Lausanne), the single-PDF and recommendation-letter mechanics, the certified-copies rule for non-Lisbon states, the C1 language thresholds and the excluded programmes.

applicant_utility.summary: Around ten of these are awarded each year: CHF 1,600 per month for the minimum statutory length of your Master's plus exemption from registration fees (only CHF 80 semester fees remain), and UNIL is blunt that this is not full funding since Lausanne costs about CHF 2,000 a month - so plan a personal contribution. One submission does two jobs: the scholarship file is also your admission application, with the same single PDF, two referee e-mails and (only for non-Lisbon-Convention countries) posted certified copies all due by 1 November. Recipients do get guaranteed FMEL housing, which matters in Lausanne's tight rental market.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Recent graduates of foreign universities with outstanding transcripts who want a UNIL Master's outside the excluded medical/law/MAS programmes and can top up roughly CHF 400+ per month themselves.
application_readiness_checklist: Check the eligible-programmes list before anything else - medicine, most law specialisms, education sciences, sport didactics, health sciences, sustainable management & technology, human taphonomy and all MAS are out
Assemble the single PDF in UNIL's exact order: CV with photo, covering letter, diplomas and transcripts (with translations), language certificate, high-school diploma, passport, CHF 200 fee receipt
Pay the CHF 200 administrative fee early by bank transfer (reason: 'Master's Scholarship - your name') and include the receipt
Ask two referees to e-mail their letters from professional addresses to mastergrants@unil.ch only AFTER your online registration - earlier letters are ignored

If your degree is from a non-Lisbon-Convention state, have the issuing university seal the certified copies in an envelope with a cover letter and post them in time for a 1 November postmark; Lisbon-state applicants must NOT send copies
Confirm your programme needs C1 English or French and hold a qualifying certificate under 2 years old (IELTS 7 / TOEFL iBT 100 / DALF C1 etc.)
common_rejection_risks: An incomplete PDF or any missing element - UNIL discards incomplete files outright
Recommendation letters sent before online registration, from private e-mail addresses, or without the candidate's full name
Applying despite being enrolled at UNIL, already in the preparatory year, or holding a UNIL master's start
Choosing an excluded programme (medicine, most of law, MAS, etc.) and discovering it late
Apostilles or notary/school/police certifications instead of the university-sealed certified true copies for non-Lisbon states - those are explicitly not accepted
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: About CHF 400+ per month beyond the scholarship (authorities estimate CHF 2,000/month for Lausanne), plus the CHF 80 semester fees, the non-refundable CHF 200 administrative fee, and FMEL rent which stays payable by the student.
document_audit: Documents not in French, German, English or Italian need authenticated translations
If the bachelor's is not yet awarded, supply all transcripts plus a precise description of remaining courses and credits
Visa-restricted nationalities should check with the Swiss embassy first - UNIL warns age and a completed first master's can make a visa difficult
alerts: The scholarship application doubles as the admission application - if the scholarship fails but the faculty admits you, you then register via the Admissions Office using the same fee
Selection Board decisions land in March with notification in early April and cannot be appealed
Withdrawing from the programme suspends the scholarship
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Online registration + single PDF + two referee e-mails (+ posted certified copies where required) by 1 November; SASME completeness check, SII formal eligibility, faculty admission decision, then the Selection Board in March.

official.deadline_note: There is no annual deadline: vacancies are published as recruitment rounds and each carries its own application deadline on the CERN careers portal. As of 2026-10-10 the programme page lists a live round, Doctoral Student Programme 2027-1 (reference TSC-2027-1/DOCT, 12 to 36 month contract, fully onsite).
official.application_cycle: Rolling, round-based recruitment (current live round: Doctoral Student Programme 2027-1, TSC-2027-1/DOCT)
official.status_note: A Doctoral Student Programme 2027-1 vacancy (TSC-2027-1/DOCT, 12-36 month contract, fully onsite) is listed as open on the official programme page.

Family supplement to the subsistence allowance, depending on individual circumstances

documents: Curriculum vitae in English or French

Family supplement to the subsistence allowance where applicable

Submit the CV (English or French) and online application before that vacancy's deadline

official.application_route: Apply to an advertised Doctoral Student Programme vacancy on the CERN careers portal before its stated deadline.
official.citizenship_residency: Nationals of CERN Member or Associate Member States only; applications from Pakistan, Lithuania, Latvia, Cyprus, Croatia and Turkey are currently excluded under the Article II.5 ceiling
official.international_eligibility: Yes for nationals of CERN Member and Associate Member States; applications from several Associate Member States are currently excluded under the Article II.5 ceiling
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: The research must contribute to a doctoral thesis in one of CERN's fields of work (physics, engineering, computing and related STEM fields)
official.research_requirement: The university must accept that the research conducted at CERN contributes to the doctoral thesis in one of CERN's fields of work
official.duration: 6-month contract renewable up to 3 years, with the possibility to spread the total over a maximum of 4 consecutive years to allow time at the student's university; the current advertised round offers 12 to 36 month contracts
official.description: CERN describes the Doctoral Student Programme as an opportunity 'designed for PhD students to engage in cutting-edge research at one of the world's most prestigious scientific institutions', run in collaboration with the student's university and paid as a monthly net allowance of 3,907 Swiss Francs.
official.program_type: Paid doctoral employment contract at an international research organisation, run jointly with a university
official.english_requirement: A good knowledge of English or French is required; the CV may be submitted in English or French.

not_confirmed: tuition_coverage: the programme is an employment contract and the official page publishes no tuition benefit, so no coverage is recorded either way
deadline_date: recruitment is round-based with each vacancy carrying its own deadline, so no single central deadline exists
verification.notes: Verified on the official CERN careers page: the CHF 3,907 monthly net allowance, health insurance with deduction, family supplement and travel on joining, leave entitlements, the 6-month contract renewable up to 3 years (spreadable over 4 consecutive years), the Member/Associate Member State nationality rule with the current Pakistan/Lithuania/Latvia/Cyprus/Croatia/Turkey exclusion under Article II.5, the university-acceptance and language requirements, the optional documents, and the live TSC-2027-1/DOCT round.

applicant_utility.summary: This is a paid employment contract, not a campus scholarship: CHF 3,907 net per month with CERN health insurance (premium deducted), possible family supplement and travel to Geneva on joining, on a 6-month contract renewable to three years and stretchable across four consecutive years so you can spend time back at your university. Your university has to agree the CERN work counts toward your thesis, and nationality is a hard gate - Member or Associate Member State nationals only, with Pakistan, Lithuania, Latvia, Cyprus, Croatia and Turkey currently blocked by the Article II.5 ceiling. Watch the careers portal rather than a calendar: rounds open and close on their own deadlines, and the live 2027-1 round advertises 12-36 month contracts.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Enrolled or incoming PhD students in physics, engineering, computing and related fields at Member/Associate Member State universities whose supervisor agrees their thesis work can be done at CERN.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm your nationality is eligible under the current Article II.5 situation before investing in the application
Get written acceptance from your university that the CERN research will count toward your doctoral thesis in a CERN field of work
Prepare a one-page CV in English or French (reference letter and transcript optional but useful)
Track the CERN careers portal for the next Doctoral Student Programme round and apply before that vacancy's own deadline
Be ready for a short-notice online interview with the hiring manager about your application and mutual fit
common_rejection_risks: Nationality exclusion (the six listed countries) - no workaround is published while the ceiling stands
A university that will not formalise that the CERN research contributes to the thesis
Missing a round because you waited for an annual deadline that does not exist
Assuming the allowance is salary-plus-tuition: it is a net allowance with insurance deducted, and no tuition benefit is published
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Anything beyond the net allowance - the health insurance contribution is deducted from it, and the programme publishes no tuition, housing or relocation support beyond possible joining travel.
document_audit: The CV must be in English or French; academic reference letter and transcript are optional but can strengthen a shortlist decision
alerts: The nationality exclusion list is time-limited and tied to the Article II.5 ceiling - it can change between rounds
Funding figures on CERN programmes are periodically revised, so re-check the CHF 3,907 net allowance against the live page before applying
The current round (TSC-2027-1/DOCT) contracts are 12-36 months even though the standard scheme is 6-month renewable
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Apply to a specific advertised vacancy on the CERN careers portal (CV + online form) before its deadline; review, possible online interview, then offer and onboarding.
